title: Sulfide solid electrolyte moisture stability
bottleneck: Sulfide solid electrolytes such as LGPS offer the highest ionic conductivities, but they react with ambient moisture to release toxic hydrogen sulfide gas. This forces all manufacturing into ultra-dry rooms, inflating capital costs, and makes cells vulnerable to any seal failure in service. No sulfide composition has achieved both top-tier conductivity and practical air stability.
why_it_blocks: Sulfides are the leading electrolyte choice for commercial solid-state batteries because of their conductivity and softness, which eases manufacturing. Moisture sensitivity is a major reason solid-state lines cost far more than conventional gigafactories, delaying mass-market EVs.
current_state: Coatings, halide doping, and oxysulfide compositions have improved stability incrementally, but dry-room requirements remain. Oxide electrolytes avoid the H2S problem yet bring their own brittleness and interface issues, so the field is split with no clear winner.
